messages:
sanjay: paging -- alert: inference-pool-us-west-2 node NotReady spike, multiple pods evicting. seeing increased 504s on the hosted API. @maria are you on call?
ops-bot: Incident created — ID INC-2026-042, severity=P2, notified: @sanjay @maria @dave. CPU/Network anomalies detected.
maria: I'm on. thanks for the heads up. silencing noisy alerts, checking kubectl get nodes and kubelet logs now.
dave: I see 3 nodes marked NotReady in autoscaling-group-gamma. kubelet restarted on nodes i-0a1b2c3, i-0d4e5f6. kernel logs show watchdog + docker/containerd OOM events.
sanjay: customer impact: elevated tail latency and some generation errors for small subset of customers pinned to that AZ. routing fallback to other regions hasn't fully buffered traffic.
emma: PagerDuty on-call is getting duplicate pages. I can coordinate customer comms if we need external notice.
maria: quick mitigation proposal: 1) cordon the two flapping nodes 2) drain pods to healthy nodes 3) temporarily scale up inference-pool-us-west-2 by +25% in other healthy AZs 4) enable routing fallback to dedicated-capacity cluster.
dave: agree. also investigate kernel OOM killer reason and GPU memory churn (we saw CUDA driver logs complaining about allocations during pod OOM). might be model memory spikes + old driver.
sanjay: executing drain on i-0a1b2c3 now (evicting 12 pods). command: `kubectl drain i-0a1b2c3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
maria: while draining, I'm tailing kubelet: `journalctl -u kubelet -f` -- seeing repeated "container runtime is down" and message: `failed to create containerd task: runc create: exit status 1: container_linux.go:...`
dave: I'm launching replacement nodes in the ASG and pinning AMI with updated nvidia-driver. `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name autoscaling-group-gamma --desired-capacity 6`
emma: routing fallback enabled to dedicated-capacity (policy id: fallback-2026-04). Monitoring for 10m for drop in error rate.
sanjay: customer impact status: several customers in the PLG tier saw increased latency, but no data loss. error rate for /v1/generate peaked at 8% for 4 minutes then trended down after drain started.
emma: filing a temporary incident notice to customers impacted by higher latency; will keep short update that teams are mitigating.
maria: observed additional pod restarts due to CUDA error: `CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED` in model-worker logs — looks like GPU memory fragmentation when containers are restarted rapidly. we should avoid all-at-once restarts.
dave: will add node-level taint to prevent new pods scheduling while kubelet stabilizes: `kubectl taint nodes i-0d4e5f6 node-flapping=true:NoSchedule`
sanjay: confirming drain complete on i-0a1b2c3. pods rescheduled successfully. error rate down to ~1.2%.
emma: PD alert deduped. customers notified. ops-bot: Update INC-2026-042: mitigation in progress, routing fallback enabled, nodes replaced, taint applied.
maria: next steps: collect kubelet/journal logs from flapping nodes, GPU driver versions, container runtime metrics, and correlate with workload memory spike windows. schedule a handoff doc for follow-up action (postmortem).
dave: created a temporary runbook note in /runbooks/incident-handbook for this event and pinned AMI rollback plan.
sanjay: handing off to morning oncall. @maria you'll take postmortem lead?
maria: I'll own the postmortem, include memory/driver upgrade plan and a mitigations checklist: bump pod disruption budget, improve graceful drain timing, and add backoff to worker restarts.
emma: leaving a short customer update ready for morning: "We saw node instability in us-west-2 which briefly increased API latency; we remediated by draining affected nodes and activating fallback routing. No data loss. A follow-up postmortem will be published."
sanjay: thanks everyone. documenting timestamps and commands executed in the incident ticket. closing this thread for live ops.
pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 acknowledged by on-call. Handoff scheduled to next shift.
